name: Kisspeptin

lead: Kisspeptin is a natural signalling peptide that tells the hypothalamus to release GnRH, which drives LH and testosterone. Its fragment kisspeptin-10 is sold as a research peptide, and testosterone-therapy forums discuss it as an alternative to hCG or gonadorelin for keeping the testes active and aiding recovery after cycles, helping maintain muscle, fullness and libido.

It binds KISS1R on GnRH neurons, increasing GnRH pulses and thereby LH and FSH from the pituitary; in men, LH stimulates testicular testosterone production. Academic trials show it raises LH in volunteers, but none tests the forum use or appearance outcomes.

paras: Forum users describe it as a research peptide used alongside testosterone replacement or after a steroid cycle, in place of hCG, usually under clinician or self-directed protocols that vary widely.

It has no approved indication, and products are unregulated research chemicals. Long-term effects of repeated self-administration have not been established in the cited trials, and effects on appearance are untested.

angle.text: Kisspeptin-10 is a hypothalamic peptide that triggers LH release, and TRT users discuss it as an hCG alternative to keep the testes producing testosterone and to aid post-cycle recovery. Academic trials show it raises LH in volunteers; use alongside TRT has not been tested.

lead: Kisspeptins are a family of neuropeptides encoded by the KISS1 gene. They act on the receptor KISS1R (GPR54) on gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons in the hypothalamus, which makes them a key upstream signal for luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and, in men, testosterone.[1][2][3] The shortest fully active fragment, kisspeptin-10, and the longer kisspeptin-54 have both been given to people in research settings.[4][5]

In testosterone-therapy and bodybuilding forums, kisspeptin-10 is discussed as a way to keep the testes signalling during testosterone replacement or after a steroid cycle, as an alternative to hCG or gonadorelin.[6][7][8] Users link this to appearance in a chain: preserved testicular function and hormone levels, better libido and mood, and continued training progress and a masculine physique. This is an off-label, non-approved use of a research peptide; no kisspeptin product is an approved medicine.

Human studies of kisspeptin are conducted mainly by academic endocrinology groups, notably at Imperial College London. They show it raises gonadotropins and testosterone in healthy men and women and in some patients with reproductive disorders, and two 2023 crossover trials in men and women with low sexual desire reported effects on brain responses and sexual behaviour.[9][10][11][12][13] The World Anti-Doping Agency added kisspeptins to its Prohibited List in 2024.[13][13] No trial found here has tested kisspeptin for muscle, physique or other appearance outcomes.
infobox: KISS1 identified 1996 in Hershey, Pennsylvania as a melanoma metastasis suppressor; peptides described 2001 [4][3]
Drives GnRH release, puberty and reproductive hormones [15][2]
Research peptide; not an approved drug

paras: The peptides derive from the KISS1 gene product and share a C-terminal RF-amide motif; they were first isolated from human placenta and shown to activate the orphan receptor GPR54.[4] The human precursor of 145 amino acids is cleaved into a 54-amino-acid peptide, which is processed further into kisspeptin-14, -13 and the active fragment kisspeptin-10.[3]

Kisspeptin stimulates GnRH release directly through GPR54.[1][14] Inactivating mutations in the receptor cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in people, and kisspeptin signalling is regarded as a gatekeeper of puberty.[15][2][16] Neurons in the arcuate nucleus that co-express kisspeptin, neurokinin B and dynorphin shape GnRH pulses.[17][18] Energy balance and stress modulate these neurons; leptin from fat tissue induces kisspeptin production, and low body fat is described as suppressing menstruation in some female athletes.[19][20][3]
Outside the brain, kisspeptin-54 rises very steeply during pregnancy, with the placenta as its source, and kisspeptin can also stimulate aldosterone and insulin secretion according to Wikipedia.[3]

In 1996 Danny Welch's group in Hershey, Pennsylvania identified a gene that suppressed metastasis in melanoma cells, and named it KISS1 after the town's chocolate Kisses.[3] The gene's products were isolated as kisspeptins and shown to be natural ligands of GPR54 in 2001.[4] In 2003 several independent groups reported that people with GPR54 mutations had hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, shifting the field from cancer to reproduction.[3] Studies in 2005 showed kisspeptin directly activates GnRH neurons and triggers pubertal onset in animals.[1][15]

Clinical work followed from the 2000s onward, including a first dose-finding administration study in adults registered in 2009 and trials in IVF triggering in 2012.[21][11] The 2020s brought intranasal, subcutaneous and prolonged-administration studies.[9][22][23][24]

On T Nation, users on testosterone replacement describe rotating kisspeptin-10 with gonadorelin because they cannot tolerate hCG,[6] or using it during post-cycle recovery with clomiphene.[25] Others describe it as a possible hCG substitute with its own drawbacks, or as something that keeps the testes 'alive' without being optimal.[26][8] One user claims it avoids the desensitisation seen with gonadorelin.[7] Posters report using it alongside growth-hormone secretagogue blends for libido.[27] These are individual reports, not controlled observations.

The appeal described in these threads is to continue testosterone therapy or finish a cycle without testicular shrinkage or loss of drive, outcomes users associate with looks, mood and training. A 2026 narrative review of peptide strategies for testosterone-therapy-induced suppression notes that such peptides may support endogenous hormone signalling but that evidence for restoring fertility is limited.[13]

sections.h: Research on libido and sexual function
paras: In February 2023 Imperial College London researchers published two randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trials in JAMA Network Open, one in 32 premenopausal women and one in 32 men, all with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. Kisspeptin increased activity in brain regions involved in sexual processing and improved behavioural measures compared with placebo; in men the report included up to a 56 percent increase in penile rigidity during an erotic video, and no side effects were reported in either group.[12] The investigators described the trials as proof-of-concept and planned larger studies.[12] Wikipedia notes that a single intravenous infusion was well tolerated in this work.[3]

A 2026 systematic review of peptides for male sexual dysfunction, covering 12 human studies in 372 men, reported that kisspeptin raised gonadotropin secretion and improved penile tumescence and desire in men with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, while noting small samples and short follow-up.[13] A 2025 consensus statement says kisspeptin is involved in arousal but that its clinical use is still under investigation.[13]

Healthy volunteers. A randomized trial found that intranasal kisspeptin rapidly raised gonadotropin levels in humans.[9] A single kisspeptin-54 injection temporarily increased LH pulsatility in healthy women.[5] A 2025 randomized trial reported that kisspeptin stimulated reproductive hormones without affecting anxiety,[10] and a randomized trial examined its acute effects on bone metabolism in healthy men.

Men, repeated administration. A 2026 single-blind placebo-controlled study in healthy men found that subcutaneous kisspeptin-10 dose-dependently raised LH, FSH and testosterone over an eight-hour infusion; continuous infusion for five days kept testosterone elevated while gonadotropins returned to vehicle levels, and 12 days of daily infusions sustained gonadotropin rises with some attenuation, with a bolus still effective afterwards.[13] A separate 2026 study of three healthy men on a 24-hour continuous infusion saw LH rise five- to eight-fold and then fall 13 to 47 percent from peak, which the authors interpret as desensitisation.[13]

Patients. Registered trials have tested kisspeptin in infertility and IVF triggering,[21] hypothalamic amenorrhea and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism,[28][29][24] and as a diagnostic probe of GnRH function.[30][11] Studies of prolonged and continuous administration are examining how responses change over time.[22][23][24]
None targets muscle building, appearance outcomes, or testosterone-therapy co-use compared with hCG in men.

The human studies above were conducted under research oversight, and the cited abstracts do not establish long-term safety of repeated self-administration. Kisspeptin has no approved medical indication and products sold online are marketed as research peptides, with purity and identity not verified by regulators. A Hacker News commenter in 2023 cautioned that kisspeptin acts on several signalling systems and that hormonal feedback loops make outcomes unpredictable.[31]

Sport. The World Anti-Doping Agency added kisspeptin-54 and its isoforms, including kisspeptin-10, and agonists such as TAK-448 to the Prohibited List in 2024 as testosterone-stimulating peptides in male athletes.[13][13] Detection researchers reported that a black-market vial of kisspeptin-10 they analysed showed no unexpected impurities but had degraded more than the reference standard.[13]

Active registered studies include subcutaneous kisspeptin in hypothalamic amenorrhea and a probe of GnRH neuronal function in health and disease.[28][30] Other projects examine kisspeptin antagonists and neurokinin-B receptor blockers as ways to turn the axis down in conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome.[2][23]
